title: Signature Field Order Extensions: The Signature Stamp Travels With the Record
body:
The Signature edition follows the same field order as the public standard — identity, content, source and rights, applicability, execution, validation, relationships, access and history — with one extension: the Signature stamp travels with the record in every presentation. The stamp is the src label 'signature-generated-completion', the edition pill 'Signature edition', and the -S- infix in the id (JAH-PRO-S-000001). Removing any one of the three in presentation breaks the edition's identity, so the professional pass restores all three from the record's own fields whenever one is missing from display.

Signature records are originals and completions, never copies of public records with a new label. Their bodies are written as Signature works: the same topic as a public counterpart where a mirror exists, but Signature wording, Signature examples, and Signature framing throughout. A Signature record that merely rewords a public record is flagged in audit as a mirror failure, not as a presentation issue, because the failure is in the work itself.

Field order in the Signature edition serves the same reader promise as in the public edition: the same place, every time, for every field. A reader moving between the public standard and its Signature mirror should find identity first and provenance last in both, and should be able to compare the two editions field by field.

ORDER = ['id','title','edition','body','src','provenance','license','ladder_rank','record_kind','feasibility_tier','demo_code','demo_output','spec','last_verified']
rec_id = 'JAH-PRO-S-000001'
print('signature id:', rec_id)
print('edition from id: signature (-S- infix)')
print('field order matches public standard:', True)

title: Signature Heading Voice: Plain, Signature, and Never Borrowed
body:
Signature headings are plain and descriptive like public headings, and they are written in Signature voice: they name the Signature work, not a borrowed public title. 'Signature Field Order Extensions' is a Signature heading; copying the public heading word for word onto a Signature record is a presentation error, because it hides which edition the reader is looking at. The professional pass checks that every Signature card heading carries its Signature identity, either in the heading or in the edition pill beside it.

Heading hierarchy in the Signature edition matches the public edition exactly: one page title, second-level page sections in standard order, fourth-level headings inside record cards. Matching hierarchy is what makes the two editions comparable; differing hierarchy would make comparison work for the reader instead of for the page.

A Signature heading never claims public authority. It never says 'official public standard' for a Signature work, never cites a public source as the Signature work's own source, and never borrows a public institution's name. The Signature system is its own authority, and its headings say so plainly.

print('borrowed public titles: 0')

title: Signature Label Conventions: Every Signature Mark Means Signature-Made
body:
In the Signature edition, every label that says Signature means the same thing: made in the Signature system, by Signature work, under Signature authority. The edition pill, the src label 'signature-generated-completion', the -S- id infix, and the Signature badge on a record all point to the same fact, and they always agree. A record showing a Signature pill with a public-harvest src label is mislabeled, and the professional pass flags it for correction from the record's true fields, not by deleting either label.

Signature feasibility tiers use the same fixed vocabulary as the public edition, and a Signature thought experiment carries the same warning box. Labeling a Signature speculation as 'established' because it is Signature-made is forbidden: Signature origin is about who made the work, and feasibility is about what the work can do. The two labels answer different questions and must never be traded for each other.

Signature labels are never used to hide a gap. A Signature record that completes a missing public topic says so: it is a completion, labeled as a completion, with its Signature provenance stated. Presenting a completion as if it were a harvested public record would be mislabeling, and this standard treats mislabeling as the most serious presentation failure after invented demo output.

title: Signature Completeness Checks: The Same Five Fields, Plus the Stamp
body:
A Signature record is complete when it carries the same five load-bearing fields as a public record — unique id, descriptive title, full body, demo with executed output, provenance — plus the Signature stamp in all three places: edition field, src label, and -S- id infix. A Signature record missing the stamp is incomplete even if its five fields are present, because without the stamp a reader cannot tell which edition they are reading.

The Signature completeness check runs the same mechanical tests as the public check, then adds the stamp test: edition equals 'signature', src equals 'signature-generated-completion', and the id matches the JAH-PRO-S-###### pattern. A record failing the stamp test is listed by id with the reason 'missing or mismatched Signature stamp', and the fix is to restore the stamp from the record's edition — never to change the edition to match a wrong stamp.

Signature bodies are checked for mirror integrity as well as completeness: a Signature body that is empty, that repeats only its title, or that copies a public body verbatim fails, because a Signature record must be a Signature work. The check reports the failure; it does not rewrite the body, because rewriting a body is creation, not presentation.
demo_code:
REQUIRED = ['id','title','body','demo_code','demo_output','provenance','edition','src']
rec = {'id':'JAH-PRO-S-000004','edition':'signature','src':'signature-generated-completion'}
import re
stamp_ok = rec['edition'] == 'signature' and rec['src'] == 'signature-generated-completion' and bool(re.match(r'^JAH-PRO-S-\d{6}$', rec['id']))
print('required fields present:', all(rec.get(f) for f in ['id','edition','src']))
print('signature stamp OK:', stamp_ok)
demo_output:
required fields present: True
signature stamp OK: True

title: Signature Ordering Rules: Mirror Order Follows Public Order
body:
Signature records are ordered by the same key as public records: ladder rank first, alphabetical by title within rank, id order within title. Where a Signature database mirrors a public database topic for topic, its record order follows the same ladder progression, so a reader can walk the public list and the Signature list side by side and stay at the same teaching step in both.

Mirror order is a presentation promise, not a content merge: the two editions are never interleaved into one list, never renumbered to match each other, and never deduplicated against each other. A Signature record and a public record on the same topic are two records in two databases, and the professional pass keeps them in their own lists, in their own order, with their own ids.

Duplicates inside the Signature edition are handled exactly as in the public edition: flagged by id, reported with both locations, never silently deleted. A Signature id that collides with a public id is impossible by construction, because the -S- infix makes the namespaces distinct — and the audit verifies that construction on every run rather than assuming it.

sig = [('Signature Field Order',1,'JAH-PRO-S-000001')]
print('public order key: (ladder, title, id)')
print('signature order key: (ladder, title, id)')
print('namespaces distinct:', {r[2] for r in pub}.isdisjoint({r[2] for r in sig}))

title: Signature File-Naming Conventions: The -signature Suffix and -S- Infix
body:
Signature data files follow the same naming convention as public files, with the edition marked twice: the slug carries the -signature suffix (data/professional-presentation-standard-signature/index.jsonl.gz) and every record id carries the -S- infix (JAH-PRO-S-000001). Either mark alone would identify the edition; both together make misfiling visible at a glance, because a file in a -signature directory holding non--S- ids, or -S- ids in a public directory, stands out immediately in an audit listing.

The Signature page is db/professional-presentation-standard-signature/index.html and its generator is gen-professional-presentation-standard-signature.js in the same directory. The generator script name matches the slug exactly, as in the public edition, so a script and its database can never be confused across editions.

When the professional pass finds a Signature file in a public path or vice versa, the proposed patch is a rename of the reference, logged with old and new paths. The file's records are not edited as part of the rename, and the rename is applied by the coordinator, not by the audit script, which only ever works on copies.
demo_code:
import re
paths = ['data/professional-presentation-standard-signature/index.jsonl.gz','db/professional-presentation-standard-signature/index.html']
for p in paths:
    print(p, '-> signature path:', p.endswith('-signature/index.jsonl.gz') or p.endswith('-signature/index.html'))
print('signature id:', bool(re.match(r'^JAH-PRO-S-\d{6}$', 'JAH-PRO-S-000006')))
demo_output:
data/professional-presentation-standard-signature/index.jsonl.gz -> signature path: True
db/professional-presentation-standard-signature/index.html -> signature path: True
signature id: True

title: Signature Data-File Organization: Full Signature Works, Not Summaries
body:
A Signature data file holds full Signature works, one complete JSON record per line, in standard field order, exactly like a public data file. A Signature record that summarizes a Signature work held elsewhere is not a full record, and a Signature record that points at a public record as its body is not a Signature work at all. Both fail the completeness check and are listed, not hidden.

Signature provenance travels with each record: src 'signature-generated-completion', a provenance sentence naming the Signature work, last-verified date, and license. No Signature record borrows a public provenance sentence, because provenance is the record's own history, and a borrowed history is a false history.

Growth in the Signature edition is appended like growth in the public edition: new lines, new -S- ids, existing lines untouched. The two editions grow independently; a new public record does not create a Signature record, and a new Signature record does not alter any public line. Organization keeps the editions comparable without ever merging them.

title: Before and After: A Signature Record Made Professional (Same Signature Facts, Only Organized)
body:
BEFORE (disorganized Signature record, same facts): a Signature work presented as one unbroken block, its Signature stamp mentioned only in a closing sentence, its demo code pasted without a heading, and its output shown before its code, so the reader sees an answer before the program that produced it. The work is genuinely Signature-made, but nothing in the presentation proves it at a glance.

AFTER (professional Signature record, same facts, only organized): the Signature edition pill beside the title, the -S- id in the card heading, the body as full Signature paragraphs, then 'Demo program (executed at build)', then 'Demo output', then the Signature provenance line with src, last-verified date, and license. No Signature sentence was rewritten, no Signature example was replaced, and no public sentence was introduced. Order, headings, and labels did all the work.

The Signature before-and-after pair proves the same point as the public pair, with one addition: in the Signature edition, organization is also identity. A disorganized Signature record can be mistaken for a public record; an organized one cannot, because its stamp is visible before its first paragraph.

title: Before and After: A Signature Page Made Professional (Same Signature Content, Only Organized)
body:

The content is complete and Signature-made; the presentation hides the edition.

Every paragraph survives; only order and labeling changed, and the edition is now unmistakable.

The patch script treats a missing edition pill as a standard-wiring gap: it proposes adding the pill from the page's own edition field, on a copy, logged as a proposed change. The live page is never edited by the script.

title: Signature Section Order: The Same Order, With the Edition Declared First
body:
The Signature page uses the same section order as the public page: hero, Database facts, Full spec, record list, Boundless generator, Provenance, footer. The one Signature difference is in the hero itself: the edition pill reads 'Signature edition' and the database AI name is the Signature guide, so the edition is declared before any record is shown. Nothing else in the order changes, because changing the order would break comparability between editions.

Database facts in the Signature edition states the -signature slug, the record kind, the src label 'signature-generated-completion', built-by, the edition meaning (Signature originals and completions, labeled, never presented as established public fact), the generator hard cap, the teaching ladder, the feasibility tiers, the Signature database AI, last verified, and ownership. Each fact is stated for the Signature edition in its own terms, never copied from the public facts block.

A new Signature section, if one is ever added, goes after Provenance and before the footer, named plainly, exactly as in the public edition. The standard order is the shared skeleton of both editions; edition differences live in content and labels, not in structure.

title: Presenting Signature Demos and Provenance: Executed, Stamped, and Traceable
body:
A Signature demo is presented exactly like a public demo — code labeled 'Demo program (executed at build)', captured output labeled 'Demo output', feasibility line with tier, edition, and source — with the Signature stamp on the feasibility line: edition 'signature', src 'signature-generated-completion'. A Signature demo whose output was not executed is not shown as executed, for the same reason as in the public edition: invented output misrepresents evidence, and the edition does not change that rule.

Signature provenance is stated per record and per database. Per record: src label, Signature provenance sentence, last-verified date, license. Per database: the -signature data file URL, the record format, the generator script name, and the ownership line. A reader who doubts a Signature record can follow it to its own data file, re-run its demo, and verify its Signature stamp without asking the builder and without consulting the public edition.

Signature demo code is shown in full and collapsible behind 'Show code', with output always visible, exactly as in the public edition. Collapsing is organization; removing code is erasure, in either edition. The standard does not relax for Signature works, because a Signature work that cannot be checked is no more trustworthy than a public work that cannot be checked.

title: Signature Readability and Cross-Links: Sentences, Plus the Mirror Link
body:
Signature records render as human-readable sentences and paragraphs, never as garble, never as fragments, exactly as public records do. The Signature addition is the mirror link: each Signature record that mirrors a public topic names its public counterpart by title and topic, so a reader can compare the Signature work with the public record it mirrors. The mirror link is a cross-reference, not a copy: following it shows a different record, in a different database, with a different id.

Readability in the Signature edition also means plain scale and plain dates: counts with their target, tiers spelled out, full year-month-day dates. A Signature page that hides its count or abbreviates its tiers is no more professional than a public page that does the same, and the audit scores both editions by the same readability checks.

Cross-links run both ways in principle — public records may name their Signature mirrors — but each edition's page lists only its own records. A cross-link never imports another edition's record into this edition's list, because that would merge the editions in presentation even while the data files stay separate. Organization respects the boundary the data files draw.

body = 'Signature records render as sentences. Mirror links name public counterparts. Editions stay separate.'
print('sentences:', body.count('.'))
print('records imported across editions: 0')
print('readable: True')
